#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#
93	# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
127	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
129	    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
130	    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
131	    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1

# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
#
# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
#
# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.

# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
zbuild_pg_resolve() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _child _self
    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_child"
        return 0
    fi
    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
    #
    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
    # about.
    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_pid"
    fi
}

# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
#
# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
    # as an option.
    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
    done
    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
_zbuild_pg_grace() {
    local _g="${1:-1}"
    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
}

# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
#
# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
#
# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
}

# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
#
# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
#
# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
#
# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
#
# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
zbuild_pg_register() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
    local _start
    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
zbuild_pg_kill() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
zbuild_pid_kill() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
fi

# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
    date +%s%N
    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"

# _orch_local_kill_slot <sig> <wrapper_pid> [inner_pid]
# Sends signal to both the wrapper PID and the inner work-unit PID (if known).
_orch_local_kill_slot() {
    local sig="$1"
    local wrapper_pid="$2"
    local inner_pid="${3:-}"

}

# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>

# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate

# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`

# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)

# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local work_unit="$3"

    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""

    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
        return 1
    fi

    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
        return 1
    }

    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"

    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.

        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &

        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
        trap - EXIT INT TERM
        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
    ) &

    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
    echo "$slot_id"
    return 0
}

# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
_orch_local_collect_results() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
    local deadline=0
    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))

    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"

        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
                _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                sleep 0.5
                _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
                break
            fi
            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
        done

        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"

    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0

    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    sleep 0.5
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
    return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Guard: a test that force-kills a runner must not undercut the engine's own
# teardown budget (#2029).
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-5 sends SIGTERM, then force-kills the
# runner after a grace period, then asserts every stage wrote its release line.
# The grace was a hardcoded `sleep 3`.
#
# The engine bounds each release hook at ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT, default **30s**
# (`core/pipeline/runner.sh:2025`), PER STAGE. Three stages release in that case,
# so teardown is entitled to take far longer than three seconds. When it did, the
# test killed the very thing it was about to assert on, and the marker came back
# EMPTY — both stages missing, not one:
#
#     ✗ [SPEC-5] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: intake build
#       no release from: intake build | marker=
#
# Reproduced deterministically by shortening the grace to 0.2s: identical
# signature. That is the mechanism — not machine load, though load is what made
# teardown slow enough to hit it.
#
# The durable invariant is not a bigger number. It is that the grace must be
# DERIVED from the budget it is protecting, so the two cannot drift apart again.
set -uo pipefail
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "exit-path tests do not undercut the engine's teardown budget (#2029)"
setup_test_env "exit-path-teardown-budget"

T="$REPO_ROOT/tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-0: the integration test exists" "$T"

# ── SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins the per-stage timeout_s: fixture ──────
# After #1801 the bound is _runner_dispatch_always_run reading template_stage_time_limit
# (the stage block's top-level timeout_s:, NOT router.timeout_s or
# ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT). The SPEC-5 block pins a _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT
# variable that feeds the template fixture, so the grace can be derived from
# the right value.
_spec5_block="$(sed -n '/SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill/,/SPEC-6/p' "$T")"
if grep -q '_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT' <<< "$_spec5_block"; then
    assert_pass "SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins the template timeout_s: fixture (_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT)"
else
    assert_fail "SPEC-1: the hard-kill case pins the template timeout_s: fixture (_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT)" \
        "not found — teardown may take an uncontrolled bound while the test force-kills far sooner"
fi

# ── SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived, not a literal ─────────────────
# The bug in one line. A literal cannot track the budget it is meant to outlast,
# and this one was 10x too small.
if grep -qE '\(\s*sleep\s+[0-9.]+\s*;\s*kill\s+-KILL' <<< "$_spec5_block"; then
    assert_fail "SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived from the release budget" \
        "hardcoded literal in \`( sleep N; kill -KILL ... )\` — cannot track the budget it protects"
else
    assert_pass "SPEC-2: the force-kill grace is derived from the release budget"
fi

# ── SPEC-3: and the derivation actually clears the worst case ─────────────
# Derived is not sufficient if the arithmetic is wrong. Three stages release on
# this path, each bounded independently, so the grace must clear 3x the per-hook
# bound. Evaluated rather than pattern-matched: the grace is an expression, and a
# guard that only recognised a literal would pass the moment someone wrote one.
_pinned="$(grep -oE '_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=[0-9]+' <<< "$_spec5_block" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
_expr="$(grep -oE '_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=\$\(\([^)]*\)\)' <<< "$_spec5_block" | head -1 | sed -E 's/^_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=\$\(\((.*)\)\)$/\1/')"
_graceval=""
if [[ -n "$_pinned" && -n "$_expr" ]]; then
    # Only our own arithmetic reaches here, and only after the two greps above
    # matched the exact shapes; nothing external is evaluated.
    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT="$_pinned"
    _graceval="$(( _expr ))" 2>/dev/null || _graceval=""
fi
if [[ -n "$_graceval" ]] && (( _graceval >= _pinned * 3 )); then
    assert_pass "SPEC-3: grace ${_graceval}s clears 3 stages x ${_pinned}s"
else
    assert_fail "SPEC-3: grace clears 3 stages x the per-hook bound" \
        "pinned='${_pinned:-none}' grace='${_graceval:-unevaluatable}' — need grace >= 3x pinned"
fi

print_test_results

13	  strategy: map

16	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
17	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
18	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed

29	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
30	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
31	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
32	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —

34	# (review_lenses-summary.md) and says whether one was flagged

38	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
39	flow:
40	  - hydrate
41	  - intake
42	  - plan
43	  - delivery_loop

45	  - pr

48	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
49	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
50	#
51	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
52	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
53	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
54	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a

56	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
57	# called.

130	    timeout_s: 600

134	# mechanical gates. #2368: the engine combines them — exit_when names every
135	# member that must pass this round; one with no outcome this round counts as

173	      - { stage: build, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
174	      - { stage: test, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }

191	  persona: product-owner

193	    destinations: [file, stdout]
194	    tail_lines: 200

209	  timeout_s: 1500

211	  # failures and the last good design — 3 runs in all.
212	  retry: 2
213	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
214	  persona: architect
215	  io:
216	    destinations: [file, stdout]
217	    tail_lines: 200
218	  router:
219	    timeout_s: 600
220	    max_turns: 0
221	
222	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────

id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

# #2367: the run's branch; {key} is the run's identity (issue-<n>). A repository
# overrides it in .zbuild/branch; ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH overrides both.
branch: zbuild/{key}

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates; the objective-gate plugin was then removed in B7 (#1139).
# #2368: the engine combines the gates by build_test_cycle's exit_when, which
# names every member that must pass; gate-aggregator is retired.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element. #2368: the engine sums the lenses up
# (review_lenses-summary.md) and says whether one was flagged
# (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED); review-aggregator is retired. The lens group is
# ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (build_test_cycle's exit_when, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds design and the build loop. Every stage sees every
# finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine never
# decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - design makes one model call per run and checks the design it wrote. One
#     that fails is `unusable`: the engine runs design again (its retry:), and
#     each run starts from the last good design and the last try's failures
#     (ADR-068 §8). A design that still fails ends the run — stop_run_on_fail:
#     build never runs on it, and another round would only repeat those tries.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  stop_run_on_fail: [design]
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── test-author (leaf, build_test_cycle member; the loop requires it) ───────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (4 model calls of 15 minutes, plus a few minutes); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3780
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as design's coverage check (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]
  # Same question design's coverage check asks of the design — "was what was asked for
  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
# mechanical gates. #2368: the engine combines them — exit_when names every
# member that must pass this round; one with no outcome this round counts as
# failed (the ADR-019 fail-closed contract). gate-aggregator is retired.
# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
# which goes round from design.
build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until every one passes
  flow:
    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff. #2370: it then checks each
    # assertion tests what its SPEC says (was spec-correspondence), and the loop
    # requires it to pass — the SPEC is design's, which it cannot re-author.
    - test-author
    # #2371: build scans its own change for secrets (was a stage of its own).
    - build
    - test
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after design's own coverage check that reads the issue; each unmet
    # requirement is a numbered finding.
    - issue-acceptance
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: test-author, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      # #2371: build must pass — it scans its own change for secrets, and a
      # build that broke scope or did not finish is not done either.
      - { stage: build, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: test, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: issue-acceptance, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue
# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: product-owner
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
    # headroom. The planner is
    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
    max_turns: 45

# ─── design (leaf, delivery_loop member) ───────────────────────────────
design:
  gate: auto
  roles: [designer]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (one 10-minute design call
  # and a 10-minute coverage call, plus a few minutes); the engine stops it
  # here. Each run is a new stage, with its own limit. The default is 900.
  timeout_s: 1500
  # ADR-068 §8: a run whose design cannot be used is run again, handed its
  # failures and the last good design — 3 runs in all.
  retry: 2
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: architect
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 600
    max_turns: 0

# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (3 rounds of 15-minute model calls, and more); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3600
  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
  persona: developer
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0

# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  # #2372: test runs the shape floor and the acceptance check over its own run,
  # and checks the assertion files against their fingerprints. ADR-036 #1188:
  # negctl_timeout_s bounds each requirement's negative-control / reachability
  # run (seconds).
  negctl_timeout_s: 60
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (the full test suite); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 2700
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
#
# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
# Convergence is owned by build_test_cycle's exit_when above;
# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
review_lenses:
  type: map
  # #2368: a lens fails on a problem the change introduced of these severities.
  fail_on: [high, critical]
  over: lenses
  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
  # from the lens's name.
  elements:
    - id: security
      persona: security
    - id: performance
      persona: performance
    - id: red-team
      persona: red-team
    - id: correctness
      persona: correctness
    - id: scope
      persona: scope
    - id: sre
      persona: sre
  roles: [review_lens]
  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
  max_parallel: 4
  on_member_error: continue
  aggregate: advisory
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
pr:
  gate: auto
  roles: [pr]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
#
# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
# abort.
#
# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
# process-group kill does not.
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.

hydrate:

  blocking: false

content.thinking:
Now I see what I need to check:

1. In simple.yaml:
   - `release` has `router.timeout_s: 30` (NOT `timeout_s: 30` at the top level!)
   - `persist` has `router.timeout_s: 120` (NOT `timeout_s: 120` at the top level!)

This is important for SPEC-5 requirements:
> `_runner_dispatch_always_run` bounds each always-run stage with `template_stage_time_limit` (`timeout_s:` 30 s for release, 120 s for persist)

So the requirement says the SPEC is that `template_stage_time_limit` should be used (which reads `timeout_s:` at the top-level stage block), and the values 30s/120s should come from this. 
The actual fix I'm converging on: move `timeout_s:` out from under `router:` to the top level of each stage block in simple.yaml, and have `_runner_dispatch_always_run` call `template_stage_time_limit` instead of the old `_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*` constants, so release ends up with `timeout_s: 30` at the top level.

Now I need to figure out what SPEC-5 actually requires checking for: it flags that I'm missing verification of the specific 30s and 120s template values, plus confirmation that `router.timeout_s` is no longer being read for this purpose. So I need to check that simple.yaml has `timeout_s: 30` at the top of the release block and `timeout_s: 120` at the top of the persist block.

For the router.timeout_s check, I need to confirm runner.sh doesn't pull timeout values from router config for always-run dispatch anymore -- I should look more closely at the `_runner_dispatch_always_run` function to verify this.

# This used to name one plugin by directory (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and
    # degrade to a no-op if it was absent — the engine knowing one plugin's path
    # is the coupling ADR-047 forbids, and a silent no-op is how #1878's sibling
    # mechanism went uninvoked without anything noticing. The list now comes
    # from the template's `always_run:`, resolved by role through the same
    # `resolve_plugin_for_role` seam every dispatch strategy uses.
    #
    # Scope stays pinned to `release` for the teardown role: free live resources
    # and delete NOTHING, so a failed run keeps all of its evidence on disk.
    # `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from any run path.
    _runner_dispatch_always_run() {
        [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" && -f "${_runner_state_file}" ]] || return 0
        [[ "${#_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN[@]}" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
        local plugins_root="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}"
        local _ar_stage _ar_safe _ar_role _ar_to _ar_dir _ar_guard
        for _ar_stage in "${_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN[@]}"; do
            _ar_safe="${_ar_stage//-/_}"
            # Per-stage, not global: the trap can be reached more than once, and
            # there is now more than one always-run stage to keep track of.
            _ar_guard="_RUNNER_AR_DISPATCHED_${_ar_safe}"
            [[ "${!_ar_guard:-0}" == "1" ]] && continue
            printf -v "$_ar_guard" '%s' 1

            local _ar_roles_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_${_ar_safe}"
            _ar_role="${!_ar_roles_var:-}"
            [[ -n "$_ar_role" ]] || continue
            # roles: is a list; an always-run stage takes the first.
            _ar_role="${_ar_role%%,*}"

            _ar_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$_ar_role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [[ -z "$_ar_dir" || ! -d "$_ar_dir" ]]; then
                # LOUD, unlike the old `[[ -d ... ]] || return 0`. An always-run
                # stage that cannot be resolved has not run, and the operator
                # needs to know that rather than infer it from a missing effect.
                eb_emit_event "stage.always_run.unresolved" "stage=$_ar_stage" "role=$_ar_role" 2>/dev/null || true

            fi

            local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
            _ar_to="${!_ar_to_var:-}"
            [[ "$_ar_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ar_to" -gt 0 ]] || _ar_to="${ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT:-30}"

            # would turn a Ctrl-C into a hang — the exact class of bug this
            # mechanism exists to prevent. A timeout BINARY cannot be used here

            # silently skip every dispatch). The bound is therefore a watchdog
            # that is CANCELLED on the normal path, so no stray `sleep` outlives
            # the run.
            #
            # `|| true` because an always-run stage's failure is recorded as an
            # event and must NEVER change the run's exit status.
            #
            # #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it.
            # Signalling the one PID reached only the outer shell: the subshell
            # running the stage hooks, and anything it spawned, lived on after
            # the run and wrote into its state minutes later. `set -m` (as the
            # router's model spawn does, #2056) makes each job a process-group
            # leader, so `kill -- -<pid>` reaches the whole tree — TERM, then
            # KILL after a short grace for a hook that traps TERM. The watchdog
            # gets its own group too, so cancelling it leaves no `sleep` behind.

                set -m
                plugin_hook_call "$_ar_dir" run "$_ar_stage" "$_runner_state_file" &
                _ar_pid=$!

                # that ignored TERM would lose its KILL when the watchdog is
                # cancelled below, so KILL the group now; a no-op when it is gone.

                kill -TERM -- -"$_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/stage-time-limit.sh — the whole-stage time limit (ADR-063, amended
# 2026-10-15). Read from the loaded template (_TPL_SOURCE_FILE, exported by
# load_template), so every dispatch arm — the map arm's generated script
# included — sees the same value.
#
# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_TIME_LIMIT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STAGE_TIME_LIMIT_LOADED=1

# Per-stage `timeout_s:` — how long the engine lets the WHOLE stage run before
# it stops it (every model call, check and retry inside it). Not router.timeout_s,
# which bounds one model call. 900 seconds (15 minutes) when unset. Read lazily
# from the template source, like template_stage_retry.
template_stage_time_limit() {
    local _tstl; template_stage_time_limit_v _tstl "$1"; printf '%s' "$_tstl"
}
# template_stage_time_limit_v <var> <stage> — the same into <var>. One read of
# the template gives every stage's limit (template_stage_time_limits_load), and
# load_template makes that read in the runner's shell, so every dispatch
# inherits it (ADR-065 §5): asked per stage, the read was redone in each
# dispatch's subshell.
declare -gA _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO=()   # "<template>\034<stage>" → its timeout_s text; "<template>\034" → read
template_stage_time_limit_v() {
    local -n _tstv="$1"
    template_stage_time_limits_load
    _tstv="${_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}"$'\034'"$2"]:-}"
    [[ "$_tstv" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || _tstv=900
}

# template_stage_time_limits_load — every stage's `timeout_s:` from the template,
# in one pass, into _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO; once per template (…_reload reads again).
# A stage's limit is its block's own `timeout_s:` one level in: the block opens
# at `<stage>:` in column 0, or two deep under `stage_definitions:`, and closes
# at the next line no deeper than its header; the first such line wins, and a
# block can open again further down. Every stage is followed at once, rule for
# rule as the per-stage reader this replaces (tests/unit/shell-work-cost-test.sh
# W5 holds the two equal).
template_stage_time_limits_load() {
    local f="${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}"
    [[ -n "$f" ]] || return 0
    [[ -n "${_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["$f"$'\034']+x}" ]] && return 0
    _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["$f"$'\034']=1
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 0
    local line lead li in_defs=0 s s1 s4 s4_was v
    local -A open=() ind=() found=()
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^stage_definitions:[[:space:]]*$ ]]; then in_defs=1; continue; fi
        lead="${line%%[! ]*}"; li=${#lead}
        s1=""; [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*):[[:space:]]*$ ]] && s1="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        (( in_defs )) && [[ "$line" =~ ^[a-zA-Z_] ]] && in_defs=0
        s4=""; (( in_defs )) && [[ "$line" =~ ^\ \ ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*):[[:space:]]*$ ]] && s4="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        s4_was="${s4:+${open[$s4]:-}}"
        for s in "${!open[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ [^[:space:]] ]] && (( li <= ind[$s] )); then unset 'open[$s]'; continue; fi
            if (( li == ind[$s] + 2 )) && [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:[[:space:]]* ]]; then
                v="${line:${#BASH_REMATCH[0]}}"
                if [[ "$v" == *#* ]]; then v="${v%%#*}"; v="${v%"${v##*[![:space:]]}"}"; fi
                _ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO["$f"$'\034'"$s"]="${v//[[:space:]]/}"
                found[$s]=1; unset 'open[$s]'
            fi
        done
        if [[ -n "$s1" && -z "${found[$s1]:-}" ]]; then open[$s1]=1; ind[$s1]=0; fi
        if [[ -n "$s4" && -z "${found[$s4]:-}" && -z "$s4_was" ]]; then open[$s4]=1; ind[$s4]=2; fi
    done 2>/dev/null < "$f"
}

# template_stage_time_limits_reload — forget the template's limits and read it
# again: load_template's call, as the file may have changed since it was read.
template_stage_time_limits_reload() {
    local f="${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" k
    [[ -n "$f" ]] || return 0
    for k in "${!_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO[@]}"; do
        [[ "$k" == "$f"$'\034'* ]] && unset "_ZB_STAGE_TL_MEMO[$k]"
    done
    template_stage_time_limits_load
}

print_test_results() {
    if [[ "${SKIP:-0}" -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo -e "  ${YELLOW}${BOLD}SKIP${RESET}"
        echo ""
        # #1063 follow-up: record this file as skipped so run-tests.sh can report
        # skips distinctly. A skipped file exits 0 and would otherwise tally as a
        # PASS, hiding platform gating (e.g. #996's skip_on_platform macos shows up
        # as a confusing "172/172 passed" with no indication 8 tests were skipped).
        [[ -n "${ZBUILD_TEST_SKIP_LOG:-}" ]] \
            && printf '%s\n' "${0##*/}" >> "$ZBUILD_TEST_SKIP_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
        exit 0
    fi
    # #600: in quiet mode, emit a single-line compact summary FIRST so the
    # pipeline operator can scan a 30-line test-stage banner instead of ~150.
    # The full multi-line block follows unchanged (no info loss for humans
    # reviewing failures).
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        if [[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}${BOLD}✓ ${PASS}/${TOTAL} passed${RESET}"
        else
            echo -e "  ${RED}${BOLD}✗ ${PASS}/${TOTAL} passed (${FAIL} FAILED)${RESET}"
        fi
    fi
    echo ""
    echo -e "${DIM}  ──────────────────────────────────────────${RESET}"
    echo ""
    if [[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}${BOLD}All $TOTAL tests passed${RESET}"
    else
